title: Document the 1.2.0 contract semantics
objective: Record one bounded documentation task that exercises every 1.2.0 addition: a human scope gate inside an agent chain, an agent-initiated block that stays with the agent that must produce the missing evidence, and execution evidence whose exit status was not captured.

requirements.description: Document the additive 1.2.0 vocabulary: predecessor references, reassessment declarations, and execution state.
Keep the documented transition set identical to the set the validator enforces.

adrReferences.note: Referenced to confirm the prohibited boundary: this documentation task must not alter the accepted authentication implementation.

acceptanceCriteria.description: The documented 1.1.0 to 1.2.0 change set matches the change actually present in both contract schemas.
Every lifecycle transition listed in the documentation is permitted by the validator and no permitted transition is undocumented.

boundaries.notes: Documentation-only task. The bracketed frontend path is listed to exercise the repository path pattern, and it is prohibited rather than allowed.

risks.description: A documentation example can drift from the schemas it describes after a later contract version.

blockers.description: The evidence QA was asked to produce for AC-02 has not been produced, so the chain cannot advance to human final approval.

nextAction.rationale: The chain ends with an agent-initiated block that names one open blocking finding and one pending blocking human decision; only the human can choose between them.

x-example-note: Synthetic 1.2.0 example. Its six handoffs include a human gate inside an agent chain, a block that is escalated to the human, and a block that stays with an agent under a declared reassessment. Evidence references describe a local session pattern and are not a substitute for the recorded CI run of a live task.
